title: Marangu Route: The Hut Route Up Kilimanjaro Explained
excerpt: Marangu is the only Kilimanjaro route with huts. It is shorter and more comfortable at night, but that does not make it the easiest way up.
body:
Marangu is the oldest route on Kilimanjaro and the only one where you sleep in huts instead of tents. That makes it popular with people who prefer a roof over their heads, especially in the rainy months. It is also sometimes called the "Coca-Cola Route", a name from the days when soft drinks were sold at the huts.

## The huts

You stay in three hut camps: Mandara (2,700 m), Horombo (3,720 m) and Kibo (4,700 m). Huts have bunk beds and mattresses, shared toilets and a dining hall. You still bring your own sleeping bag. Huts are shared with other climbers, so sleep can be noisy.

## Five or six days

Marangu is often sold as a five-day climb. We do not recommend that. Going up and down the same trail quickly gives little time to acclimatise, and success rates on five days are clearly lower. Six days, with an extra night at Horombo and a walk to Zebra Rocks, makes a real difference.

## Up and down the same way

Marangu is the only route where you descend on the same trail you climbed. Some people like the familiarity; others miss the variety of the southern routes.

## Who Marangu suits

- Climbers who prefer huts to tents.
- Travellers in the rainy seasons (April–May, November).
- People who want a straightforward, well-marked route.

If scenery and acclimatisation matter more than comfort at night, [Lemosho](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/) or [Machame](/blog/kilimanjaro-machame-route-guide/) are usually better choices.

## Summit night on Marangu

From Kibo Hut you climb steep scree to Gilman's Point on the crater rim, then follow the rim to Uhuru Peak. It is a long night either way; read [what summit night is like](/blog/kilimanjaro-summit-night/).
